text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is considered high (hypertension) when it is consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg according to the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

snippet_highlighted_words: consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic (top number) and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic (bottom number).
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 1 Hypertension (High): 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension (High): 140 mm Hg or higher systolic, or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic.
Severe Hypertension / Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic.
Systolic (top number): Measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart beats.
Diastolic (lower number): Measures the pressure in your arteries when your heart rests between beats.
You can be diagnosed with high blood pressure if either number meets the threshold for Stage 1 or Stage 2, even if the other number is normal.

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do in a Crisis

list.snippet: Severe Hypertension without symptoms: Recheck your blood pressure after a few minutes. If it remains over 180/120 mm Hg, contact your doctor immediately.
Hypertensive Emergency (with symptoms): If a reading over 180/120 mm Hg is accompanied by chest pain, shortness of breath, sudden confusion, vision changes, or numbness, call 911 immediately.
